StateBench: Testing how language models track state changes over long documents We're introducing StateBench, a benchmark for long-context state tracking—how well language models keep track of information about entities in long documents as they evolve. To this end, we developed the StateBench benchmark to capture state-tracking problems of different complexity, which we used to evaluate the differences between language models with different architectures. We find that recurrent and hybrid models can generalize much farther than transformers when trained directly on these tasks, while frontier models including Gemini 3.8 Flash, Claude Opus 5.5, and GPT-6 Sol and Luna still break down on harder forms of state tracking as inputs grow longer.
